policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV reads the singular "let thy word ... be verified" (with singular "which thou spakest"), matching the qere singular construct דברך rather than the ketiv plural דבריך.
ASV reads "the house which I have built for thy name" in Solomon's own voice, matching the qere 1cs בניתי rather than the ketiv 2ms בנית ("thou hast built").
